pattern: (lodging|sales) tax[^.]{0,160}less than 90 (continuous )?days|less than 90 (continuous )?days[^.]{0,160}(lodging|sales) tax|\btaxes a rental as lodging\b
struck: South Carolina taxes a rental as lodging when it is rented to the same guest for less than 90 days in a row.
use: South Carolina charges its lodging tax when a home is rented to the same guest for less than 90 days in a row, unless the home is rented fewer than 15 days in the year.

struck: Between Kings Highway and the ocean in Myrtle Beach, a building of more than two units built or used for nightly stays may not be leased for 90 days or more.
use: Myrtle Beach adopted a short-term rental conversion overlay, Ordinance 2024-69, on December 10, 2024.

pattern: North Myrtle Beach[^.]{0,200}\bonly a business license\b|\bonly a business license\b[^.]{0,200}North Myrtle Beach|North Myrtle Beach[^.]{0,120}nightly rentals across the city
struck: North Myrtle Beach allows nightly rentals across the city with no special zoning or permit, only a business license renewed each year and the lodging taxes.
use: North Myrtle Beach requires no special zoning or permit for a short-term rental: a business license renewed each year, the lodging taxes, and its trash, parking, noise and occupancy rules.

struck: The city held workshops on new rules from November 2024 to September 2025 and has adopted none.
use: The council has held workshops and public sessions on new rules since late 2024; the page lists no new rule.

struck: In Conway, the code's only nightly-rental use, a commercial short-term rental of up to 90 days, is allowed in three downtown districts.
use: Conway's code allows a commercial short-term rental (one family, no more than 90 days) only in its Core Commercial, Central Business and Waccamaw Riverfront districts. A bed and breakfast home, where the host lives on site, is a separate use.

struck: So outside the towns, a subdivision's recorded rules decide.
use: Horry County's zoning sets no limit on how long a home outside the towns may be rented. A subdivision's recorded rules can.

struck: In unincorporated Georgetown County (Murrells Inlet, Litchfield, the south end of Garden City), a tourist home is allowed in the General Resort Residential district.
use: In unincorporated Georgetown County (Murrells Inlet and Litchfield), a tourist home is a conditional use in the General Resort Residential district.

struck: Senate Bill 442 would confirm their power to ban them.
use: S.442 would expressly allow them to ban short-term rentals. Neither bill has left committee.

struck: What a house resold for in each area in the year to September 2026, at the middle: Murrells Inlet about $610,000; Pawleys Island and Litchfield about $650,000.
use: What a house sold for at the middle in the year to September 2026 (resales in Horry County; every recorded sale in Georgetown County): Murrells Inlet about $610,000; Pawleys Island and Litchfield about $650,000.

struck: In Longs, 280 of 607 house sales in the year (46 percent) were a builder's first sale.
use: In Longs, at least 280 of 607 house sales in the year (46 percent) were a builder's first sale, by our list of builder sellers.

struck: HUD's figure is about the 40th percentile of rent plus utilities, so about 4 in 10 such rentals cost less.
use: HUD's figure is its estimate of rent plus tenant-paid utilities for a standard 3-bedroom, set for the ZIP code.

struck: The tax on a rental at the 6 percent rate, a year, on each area's middle house (2026 rates): Murrells Inlet about $9,200; Pawleys Island and Litchfield about $9,200.
use: The tax at the 6 percent rate on each area's middle house. For Murrells Inlet and Pawleys Island it uses Georgetown County's current estimate.

struck: Before fees (Horry about $89.40 on most bills).
use: Before fees, which differ from bill to bill.

struck: So a rental's bill is about three times a resident's.
use: Outside city limits, a rental's tax bill is about 3.3 times a resident's on the same house; in the towns it differs.

struck: Nightly income by beach town: Murrells Inlet about $38,400, Surfside Beach $35,500, Garden City $33,900, North Myrtle Beach $28,700. Occupancy runs about 30 to 38 percent of nights.
use: (cut it: vendor estimates, not a primary source; link /invest/airbnb-income/)

struck: A June month earns about 2.5 to 3.3 times a January month: Myrtle Beach $4,878 against $1,466.
use: (cut it: vendor estimates, not a primary source; no month figures)

struck: Condos about $400 to $425 inland.
use: Condos about $375 to $425 inland.

pattern: \b16,300\b|\b5\.4 percent\b|North Myrtle Beach rented by the night
struck: A condo in North Myrtle Beach rented by the night: about $16,300 left before cleaning, management, utilities, furniture, insurance and any loan, about 5.4 percent.
use: (cut the nightly side: row 26 is struck)

struck: Condos in a sound building whose owner must sell are where most fix-and-hold deals turn up.
use: Most of the best BRRRR candidates we see are lower-value homes inland toward Longs or Little River, or condos in a stable building with a distressed owner.

pattern: \bearned about \$[\d,]+ each\b|\$[\d,]+ each a year, on average
struck: Nightly rentals in Garden City earned about $34,000 each a year, on average.
use: In the rental data's Garden City Beach area, the average nightly rental took in about $34,000 a year, before costs.

pattern: ^\s*In the city, the average nightly rental
struck: In the city, the average nightly rental earned about $21,000 a year, the least of the six beach areas.
use: In the rental data's Myrtle Beach area, the average nightly rental took in about $21,000 a year, the least of the six beach areas.

pattern: nightly rental took in, city average|\bcity's average for every nightly rental\b
struck: Its income is the city's average for every nightly rental, houses and condos of every size, not this condo's.
use: Its income is a rental-data company's estimate of the average Airbnb listing in its North Myrtle Beach area, houses and condos of every size, not this condo's.

struck: A nightly rental there took in about $20,000 to $38,000 on average in the past year, before costs.
use: A rental-data company estimates that the average nightly rental there took in about $21,000 to $38,000 in a year, before costs.
